mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations for consumer-facing equities and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial sector equities and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% in the same month signals a dual tightening of monetary and cost pressures, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages in the same month signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) above 63% for three consecutive months signals broader labor supply expansion, which moderates wage growth and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days via improved cost discipline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS rising while implied participation > 63% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which lifts earnings for retail and service equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
